subject: Header masking & PoC scope — logging, trace IDs, and DPA requests
messages:
From: Carolyn Mills <carolyn.mills@healthbridge.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2027 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Logging / header capture — follow-ups from today

Hi Jonas / Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — helpful to see the routing and fallback capabilities. A couple of follow-ups from our security and infra teams around logging and PII handling that we need to qualify before procurement:

1) Request / response logs: does Redwood retain full request/response payloads by default? If so, what controls exist to prevent storing sensitive fields (PII) in production logs?

2) Headers & trace IDs: we currently surface trace IDs from our front-end. Do you recommend hashing those at ingest, stripping them, or storing them in a separate, encrypted index? We need to avoid storing raw identifiers tied to users.

3) Retention & residency: our compliance team requires EU residency for logs and a maximum searchable retention of 90 days for request-level telemetry. Can you confirm residency options and retention enforcement?

4) Evidence: can you share any SOC 2 / encryption / key management artifacts or a link where we can review them?

Attached: sample-logging-schema.pdf (shows the fields we currently collect).

Next steps — our CISO would like a brief PoC plan (1–2 weeks) that demonstrates: a) request/response redaction rules in action, b) an approach to handling trace IDs (hashing strategy), and c) enforcement of EU-only storage for logs.

Can you confirm feasibilty and an estimated timeline? Also loop in whoever will own the PoC on your side.

Thanks,
Carolyn
Carolyn Mills
Head of Platform Security, HealthBridge
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Carolyn Mills <carolyn.mills@healthbridge.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2027 17:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Logging / header capture — follow-ups from today

Carolyn — really appreciate the clear list. Quick post-call recap and proposed next steps below.

Recap of what we heard from HealthBridge:
- No raw customer-identifiable IDs stored in logs (including trace IDs).
- EU residency required for logs; retention searchable <= 90 days.
- Need PoC demonstrating redaction/hashing and residency enforcement.

Redwood notes / proposals:
- Default behavior: our audit/request logs capture request metadata and a configurable request/response payload snapshot. That snapshot can be trimmed at ingest via a redaction pipeline. We have three common approaches:
  • Field-level redaction: drop or mask configured JSON keys at ingestion.
  • Upstream hashing: apply per-tenant one-way hash to specified header values (we recommend salted HMAC with tenant-specific salt).
  • Post-ingest pseudonymization: store an opaque token in logs and keep mapping in an encrypted index (more complex, heavier ops).

- Recommendation for trace IDs: one-way HMAC with per-tenant salt stored in KMS (no raw values retained). This approach preserves linkage across logs for debugging while preventing reversal to original ID.

- Retention & residency: in Redwood Dedicated/Private setups we can guarantee EU-only storage and enforce retention windows. For Hosted, we provide region pinning for log storage and an automated expiry job that purges entries after X days (we will show this in the PoC).

Attachments: redwood-logging-options.pdf (short matrix of pros/cons per approach).

Proposed PoC scope (1 week, condensed):
1) Ingest sample traffic (you provide sample-logging-schema.pdf) into an EU tenant.
2) Implement a redaction rule set that strips PII fields and hashes trace IDs with a tenant KMS-backed salt.
3) Show search/query results limited to 90-day window and demonstrate purge.
4) Deliver a short evidence pack (KMS config, key rotation policy excerpt, SOC 2 pointer).

Owners: Jonas Weber (solutions lead) — will run the PoC with Karthik.
Estimated timeline: start week of Dec 6, deliverable by Dec 13 (one-week PoC).

Questions / asks for HealthBridge before we start:
- Confirm EU-only residency is acceptable (region: eu).
- Provide a scrubbed sample payload (or confirm we can use the attached sample).
- Legal contact for DPA / contractual asks.

If that all looks good I'll put together a tighter SOW and schedule the engineering kick-off.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
From: Carolyn Mills <carolyn.mills@healthbridge.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Susan Patel <susan.legal@healthbridge.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Dec 2027 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Logging / header capture — follow-ups from today

Thanks Jonas — that approach sounds reasonable. A few clarifications from infra/legal below.

- Trace IDs: we cannot allow raw trace IDs to be stored. Per-team acceptance criteria is one-way hashing with per-tenant salt. Important: the salt must be tenant-scoped and stored in our KMS or an approved Redwood-managed KMS that supports customer-owned keys.

- Retention: 90 days max for searchable logs, with WORM-style immutable archival (encrypted) beyond that for compliance. Searchable retention must be enforced server-side — not a manual policy.

- Residency: EU-only for both searchable logs and any archival copies.

- Evidence: Susan (cc'd) is our legal lead and will handle the DPA and encryption warranty language. Susan — can you share the DPA template and confirm whether Redwood can sign with standard redlines?

Attached: dpa-request.docx (legal template).

If we can get the PoC to show HMAC hashing with per-tenant salt + EU residency + automated purge in the timeframe you suggested, we'll push this through procurement quickly.

—Carolyn
Carolyn Mills
Head of Platform Security, HealthBridge
